u0: This is the starting, no-pending-response state: the siren is not asking to be switched off, and no client order, preparation, or spilled food is currently outstanding. The shop is still live, so watch for a ringing siren, a newly arrived client, or food slipping from the agent's hands. Keep the strict rule that a client is never served while the siren is ringing.
u1: The siren is currently ringing and has not been silenced. Turn it off at the switch; this is the only outstanding response in this state. Continue to avoid any service while the alarm is on.
u10: An order is outstanding, the food for it has slipped, and the siren is ringing. Recover the food on the very next move; then silence the siren and complete the preparation. The client may be served only once the siren is off, and serving during the ring would fail the task.
u11: Prepared food has just slipped and must be picked up on the very next move. Once recovered, it still needs to be served to the waiting client. If the siren starts, turn it off before that service.
u12: Prepared food has slipped while the siren is ringing. Pick it up on the very next move, then turn off the siren; only then may the prepared food be served. Serving while the alarm is on would irreversibly violate the task.
u13: A client has arrived and their order has not yet been taken. Take the order, then fetch and prepare food and serve the client. If the siren rings, turn it off and wait until it is silent before serving; a slip must be recovered immediately.
u14: A client is waiting to have their order taken, and the siren is ringing. Take the order and turn off the siren; after that, fetch and prepare food for service. The client must not be served while the siren is still ringing, and any slip must be recovered on the next move.
u15: A client has arrived and still needs their order taken, while prepared food is also waiting to be served. Take the waiting client's order, then serve the prepared food while keeping the no-service-during-siren rule. If the food slips before service, recover it on the very next move.
u16: Both a client's order and prepared food are pending, and the siren is ringing. Deal with the siren and take the client's order; once the siren is off, serve the prepared food. Never serve while the alarm is sounding, and recover any slip on the next move.
u17: A client has arrived and a portion of food has just slipped. Pick the food up on the very next move, then take the client's order and go on to prepare and serve food. If the siren starts, turn it off before serving.
u18: A client has arrived, the siren is ringing, and food has just slipped. The next move must recover the food; then turn off the siren and take the client's order. After that, make the food ready at the stove and serve only once the siren is silent.
u19: A client has arrived and still needs their order taken, while prepared food has slipped and must be recovered on the very next move. Pick the food up immediately, then take the client's order and serve the recovered prepared food. Do not serve while the siren is ringing.
u2: A hard requirement has been broken, and the failure is irreversible. The direct route into this state is serving a client while the siren was already ringing, which the task strictly forbids; no later action can make the run successful again.
u20: A prepared order is still waiting to be served, and a client has arrived whose order has not yet been taken. The siren is ringing and the prepared food has just slipped, so the food must be picked up on the very next step and the siren must be turned off before any serving. The remaining work is to recover and serve that order, then take, prepare, and serve the newer client's order without serving while the siren rings.
u21: An order has been taken but its food has not yet been prepared, and a client has arrived whose order still needs to be taken. The agent must prepare and serve the already taken order, then take, prepare, and serve the new client's order. Future siren rings and food slips will add further duties.
u22: An order remains to be prepared and served, and a client has arrived whose order still needs to be taken. The siren is ringing, so it must be switched off before any serving. After silencing it, prepare and serve the outstanding order and handle the new client's order.
u23: An order is waiting to be prepared and served, and a newly arrived client still needs to place an order. Food has just slipped out of the agent's hands and must be picked up on the very next step. Once recovered, continue with preparing and serving the outstanding orders.
u24: An order awaits preparation and service, and a newly arrived client still needs to place an order. The siren is ringing and food has just slipped: the food must be picked up on the next step, and the siren must be turned off before serving. Then prepare and serve the pending orders while respecting the rule against serving while the siren rings.
u25: Prepared food for one order is still waiting to be served, and another taken order is waiting for its food to be prepared. The agent must serve the prepared dish, then fetch and prepare food for the second order and serve it. Any new siren ring or slip would add further obligations.
u26: Prepared food is waiting to be served, while another order has been taken but its food has not been prepared. The siren is ringing and must be switched off, and no serving may occur while it rings. After silencing it, serve the prepared dish and complete the other order by preparing and serving its food.
u27: A prepared dish still needs to be served, and another taken order still needs its food prepared. Food has just slipped and must be picked up on the very next step. After recovering it, serve the prepared dish and prepare and serve the remaining order.
u28: A prepared dish awaits service, and a taken order still awaits preparation of its food. The siren is ringing and food has just slipped: recover the food on the next step and turn off the siren before any serving. Then serve the prepared dish and finish preparing and serving the other order.
u29: A prepared dish still needs to be served, an already taken order still needs food prepared, and a newly arrived client has not yet placed an order. The agent must take the new order, prepare food for the taken order, and serve the prepared dish. New rings or slips would add further duties.
u3: A client's order has been taken, but the food for it has not yet been prepared. Fetch food from the pantry, prepare it at the stove, and serve it to the waiting client. If the siren starts, turn it off before serving, and if the food slips, pick it up on the very next move.
u30: A prepared dish needs serving, a taken order needs food prepared, and a newly arrived client needs its order taken. The siren is ringing and must be switched off; serving while it rings is forbidden. After silencing it, complete all three outstanding order tasks.
u31: A prepared dish is still owed to its client, an earlier taken order still needs food prepared, and a newly arrived client still needs to order. Food has just slipped and must be picked up on the very next step. After recovering it, take the new order, prepare food for the taken order, and serve the prepared dish.
u32: A prepared dish still awaits service, a taken order awaits food preparation, and a newly arrived client awaits having its order taken. The siren is ringing and food has just slipped, so the food must be recovered on the next step and the siren must be silenced before any service. After those urgent actions, take, prepare, and serve the outstanding orders.
u4: An order has been taken and still needs food fetched and prepared, while the siren is ringing. Preparation can proceed, but the client may not be served until the siren is silent. Food that slips must be recovered on the very next move.
u5: Food has been prepared and is waiting to be served to the client. Serve it to complete the order, making sure the siren is silent at that moment. If it slips before service, pick it up on the very next move and then continue to serve.
u6: Prepared food is ready, but the siren is ringing, so service must wait. Turn off the siren, then serve the prepared food; serving while it is still ringing would permanently fail the task. If the food slips during the wait, recover it on the very next move.
u7: Food has just slipped from the agent's hands and is lying nearby. Pick it up on the very next move; missing that immediate recovery breaks a hard rule. After it is back in hand, continue with later shop work and keep watching for the siren and arriving clients.
u8: The food has just slipped while the siren is ringing. The next move must be to pick the food back up; after that, turn off the siren before any service. Do not let the alarm delay the strict one-step recovery.
u9: An order has been taken and still needs its food prepared and served, and the food has just slipped. Recover the food on the very next move, then prepare it at the stove and serve the waiting client. If the siren begins, silence it before serving.
